business_summary.text: Siemens Energy India Limited is a leading provider of conventional and renewable energy technology, including gas and steam turbines, hybrid power plants, transformers, and grid technologies.

call_points.text: Management does not provide forward guidance; investors should track order backlog and book-to-bill.
Power transmission backlog rose 27.5% to ₹125 Bn, driven by grid expansion and export orders.
Operating margin improved 160 bps to 20.7%, driven by operating leverage and higher export mix.
Power generation margin expanded to 21.3% from 17.7%, aided by economies of scale and fixed cost synergies.
The company remains debt-free and funds expansions from internal accruals.
Order intake is volatile due to project-based nature; H1 new orders fell to ₹65 Bn from ₹72 Bn last year.
Export growth depends on parent Siemens Energy's decisions to leverage Indian capacity.
STATCOM market was muted in H1FY26, but management expects new orders as renewable integration accelerates.
Data center opportunity in India is currently limited to power transmission; no captive gas turbine demand yet.
**Expansions:** ongoing Q1-announced projects are a ₹7.4 Bn transformer expansion at Kalwa and a ₹20.6 Bn greenfield transformer factory at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

operating_notes.text: Order backlog reached ₹18,433 Cr as of March 31, 2026, up 22.2% YoY.
H1 FY26 order backlog stood at ₹18,430 Cr, up 22.2% YoY, while new orders fell to ₹66.6 Bn from ₹74.7 Bn in H1 FY25.
H1FY26 service revenue was ₹12 Bn, 27% of total revenue.
Order backlog at H1FY26 was ₹184 Bn, up 22.2% YoY, with book-to-bill of 1.5.
Power transmission backlog ₹125 Bn (+27.5% YoY); power generation backlog ₹59.2 Bn (+12.4% YoY).
Export contribution increased to 21.4% in 9M FY26.
Raw material cost decreased by 11.2% YoY to ₹418.2 Cr in Q1FY27.
Finance cost decreased by 35.2% YoY to ₹9.2 Cr in Q1FY27.
Presentation at J.P. Morgan India Conference highlights > USD 300 million committed capex for manufacturing capacity expansion.
Supreme Court of Russia rejected appeal against St. Petersburg Arbitration Court order directing payment of ₹44.38 Cr (USD 5.17M) plus 8% p.a. interest from 30 May 2025.

Siemens Energy India Limited shared the audio recording of its Analysts/Institutional Investors call held on May 15, 2026, via its website.
